meta.note: World commodity supply chains. Metals: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 (data year 2025, mostly estimates; prev = 2024). Energy: EIA international statistics, top 40 countries per list with the remainder as iso3 OTH. Uranium: World Nuclear Association. 'OTH' rows are 'other countries' and are not in the countries map. Shares are fractions of the stated world total. Trade rows from un_comtrade are destination shares of partner-reported import value in 2024 (mirror data: misses non-reporting importers and transshipment). Fields are omitted when unsourced.

commodities.name: Cobalt
commodities.basis: mine production, cobalt content, metric tons

trade.what: cobalt intermediates incl. crude hydroxide, mattes, unwrought metal (HS 810520)
trade.basis: share of partner-reported import value (mirror data)

commodities.end_use_basis: US (USGS MCS 2026). Globally the leading use is lithium-ion batteries: USGS notes China is the leading consumer, primarily for batteries, but gives no global share.
key_inputs: Byproduct of copper mining (DRC, Zambia) and nickel mining (Indonesia HPAL, Russia, Canada, Australia): cobalt supply follows host-metal economics
Sulfuric acid and sulfur for leaching (IEA 2026 flags acid cost spikes)
Chinese refineries that convert DRC hydroxide to sulfate and metal
Trucking and rail corridors from Katanga to Durban, Dar es Salaam, Lobito
commodities.notes: DR Congo mined an estimated 74% of world cobalt in 2025 and Indonesia 14% (USGS). DRC banned exports in February 2025 and replaced the ban in October 2025 with quotas: 18,125 t for the rest of 2025 and up to 96,600 t per year in 2026 and 2027, well under half of mine output. IEA reports cobalt prices rose about 130% between January 2025 and April 2026 and now projects a supply gap. China refines about three quarters.
